text:
joel: quick RFC follow-up — i'm posting the proposed approach for service identity zoning and API key evolution. tl;dr: introduce zone-scoped service identities + short-lived tokens, keep org-keys readable but deprecated for write/privileged ops. looking for concerns and rollout ideas.

maria: curious — how do we handle existing customers that have hardcoded org keys in infra? big risk if we flip too fast.

joel: yep. migration plan idea: dual-issuance (shadow tokens) + traffic tagging. new tokens will be `zone` scoped (e.g., billing, inference, analytics). org-keys remain valid for read-only by default, and write/critical endpoints will require zone svc tokens after canary.

sam: runtime/compat question: what does the header look like? do we force jwt introspection for every request? that could add p99.

joel: prototype header (for clarity):
```
Authorization: Bearer rwd-svc:zone=billing:svc=svc-42:exp=2026-09-01T00:00Z
```
we want an opaque token backed by an introspection cache at the edge (TTL 5s) to avoid heavy introspection. also allow signed JWTs for private deployments where introspection not desired.

tara: product concern — partners hit our billing api via org keys today. if we put write ops behind zone tokens, we need a migration narrative + partner playbook. also need to surface errors cleanly (401 vs 403).

lena: security notes — rotation and revocation are key. propose: all new svc tokens have built-in TTL (max 90d, encourage 24h ephemeral via client creds). support immediate revocation via revocation list propagated to edges. HSM/KMS for signing keys.

joel: migration runway idea:
1) deploy token issuer and an introspection endpoint (internal).
2) support dual acceptance at edges: accept org-key or zone-token; tag traffic source.
3) shadow-issue zone-tokens for org-key owners and emit telemetry (token pairs).
4) after 60d of telemetry, flip specific sensitive endpoints to require zone-tokens.
5) provide a `proxy-agent` pattern for legacy infra that can't rotate — short-lived proxy tokens created by customer-managed agent.

sam: ops: for step 2, can we wire routing policies so we only check introspection for canary regions? avoid global perf hit. and we should batch introspection lookups in runtime layer.

maria: metrics to track: percent of traffic using zone-tokens, auth failure delta post-flip, number of shadow-token issuances, partner opt-in rate. also add a migration flag in console per-customer. :bar_chart:

joel: agree. implementation notes: SDKs will add helpers `refreshServiceToken()` and a migration tool `rwd-key-mgr shadow-issue --org KEY`. will also need API to list active tokens and their zones.

lena: one more security edge: cross-zone calls — e.g., inference -> billing. do we allow zone-to-zone service identity delegation or require a broker? recommendation: use short-lived delegation tokens minted by a trusted broker with scoped claims.

joel: yup that's the broker pattern i prefer. prevents lateral blast radius. we should document and add a lightweight broker service that enforces policy.

auth-bot: policy-service: zone-auth v0.3 deployed to staging (automated note).

maria: sounds good. timeline suggestion: RFC + implementation plan this week, staging rollout next sprint, 60d shadow collection, then progressive enforcement. open question: default deny timeline for org-keys for write endpoints.

joel: proposed default-deny for write endpoints 90 days after GA of staging tests. volunteers to help draft the customer migration doc and SDK patches? i'm available for the broker/proxy design.

sam: i'll take the edge runtime changes (introspection cache + batched lookup).

lena: i'll own revocation + KMS integration.
tara: i'll draft partner comms and console flags.

joel: thanks — i'll put a short PR with the migration checklist and a follow-up meeting invite (📅). please add any immediate concerns here. :eyes:
